title: Inference Endpoint Compatibility & Launch Gates: capability bundles, signature shims, and launch checklist
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: define a single PRD that governs the compatibility surface and launch gates for hosted API endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). This ticket captures API signature compatibility shims, a capability-bundling approach (minimal / standard / advanced), explicit acceptance criteria across behavior, telemetry, billing, and rollout controls, and a prescriptive launch checklist to reduce cross-team risks. The goal is to enable customers to switch to the new unified surface with minimal code changes while preserving performance and observability guarantees. This doc intentionally focuses on operational compatibility (signatures, headers, error codes), quality compatibility (model-level behavior and regression detection), and economics (token accounting and per-route cost visibility).
scope: Define stable API contract for 4 surfaces: chat, completions, embeddings, rerank
Design compatibility shim for common signature variations (legacy params, casing, typed vs. untyped JSON)
Specify capability bundles (minimal, standard, advanced) and per-bundle feature gates
Required SDK changes and deprecation window for legacy clients
End-to-end acceptance tests including latency and throughput baselines
Telemetry and billing reconciliation spec (per-request token accounting + CDN edge attributions)
Canary routing plan with SLO monitoring and automatic rollback triggers
Migration guide and sample code for customers (JS/Python)
out_of_scope: Changes to private / on-prem control plane deployment flow
Deep model architecture changes or model retraining
requirements: API: single /v1/inference endpoint supports mode param (chat|completion|embedding|rerank) and retains backward-compatible aliases for existing endpoints
Signature shim: incoming request normalization layer that accepts snake_case / camelCase / PascalCase and common legacy param names for 12 months
Structured output: preserved when model returns tool calls or JSON blobs; runtime must offer a strict schema-validation toggle per-route
Embeddings: return dimensionality, model_name and a stable vector schema; embedding length migrations must return a compatibility warning header
Rerank: deterministic scoring schema with floating-point tolerances documented and unit tests included
Billing: token usage must reconcile to existing per-token billing within +/- 0.5% on canonical workloads
SDK: JS and Python SDKs must include compatibility helpers and feature-detection APIs by GA
Observability: per-route breakdowns in Console (latency p50/p95, token cost, error rate) available in the GA quadrant
Rollout: support for canary percentage routing and auto-fallback to pre-unified endpoints
acceptance_criteria: Contract: API spec (OpenAPI + example requests) published and validated by integration tests against JS/Python SDKs
Backward compatibility: 95% of active internal customers' canonical requests function without code changes when proxying through shim (sample test-suite provided)
Performance: p95 latency for standard bundle within 1.15x of current endpoint baseline under synthetic replica of customer traces
Stability: error rate under 0.5% for traffic in canary over a 72-hour period before increasing rollout
Quality parity: a regression check harness passes for 10 representative prompt families across chat/completions that capture hallucination / instruction-following metrics
Billing parity: token accounting reconciles within +/-0.5% compared to current invoicing on two customer traces and internal benchmarks
Telemetry: Console surfaces for token/cost per-route, p50/p95 latency, and model-level throughput are visible and tested
Docs: migration guide, API reference, and SDK changelog published and linked from Console onboarding
Security: security_review_required set and review completed; request headers maintain existing auth flows (API key/managed tokens)
launch_checklist: API spec file merged and version-tagged in repo
Compatibility shim deployed to staging with feature flag
Canary config created (1%, 5%, 25% steps) and smoke tests for each step
SDK releases (JS v2.4.0, Python v1.9.0) published with migration helpers
E2E test-suite run against staging using representative customer traces
Billing reconciliation run and financial sign-off from RevOps
Console dashboards validated with synthetic traffic and real traces
Runbook and rollback playbook published and shared with SRE on-call
Customer migration emails and deprecation timeline posted to docs
Legal & Compliance sign-off checklist completed for data retention and headers
rollout_plan: Start with internal tooling and low-traffic customers in a mirrored canary for 2 weeks. Progress through staged percentages (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%) with at least 48 hours and stability gates between each step. At each gate validate acceptance criteria automatically and require manual approval to continue. Provide automatic rollback to legacy endpoints on breach of defined SLOs (p95 latency, error rate, billing delta). After 30 days of stable GA, begin deprecation window for legacy aliases with a 12-month notice period.
